advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the intended contract that a trailing/embedded `--help`/`-h` in write-command free text is captured as help (no write), and that the `--` escape hatch is documented for callers who need the literal.
evidence: Docstring at lines 141-144 acknowledges: 'A --help/-h meant as the value of a value-taking option ... is likewise read as a help request here; passing such a literal is an unsupported edge'

Test at tests/.../test_create_help_no_write_b8de.py asserts `["create", "task", "a title", "--help"]` shows usage and writes nothing — confirming a trailing --help after a real title now suppresses the write
advisory.finding: The broadened help scan intercepts a `--help`/`-h` token appearing as legitimate free-text value data for write commands (e.g. a comment body, edit field value, or ticket title later in argv), silently emitting usage and performing no write instead of storing the intended literal. Previously only `rest[0]` was intercepted, so `rebar comment <id> --help` (with `--help` as body) or `rebar create task "a title" --help` would have reached the handler; now they are captured as help.
scenarios: A user runs `rebar comment <id> --help` intending '--help' as the comment text
A ticket title or edit value legitimately contains the token '--help' or '-h' without a preceding `--`

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an end-to-end `_cli.main` test asserting a help flag after `--` (e.g. `create task -- --help`) is NOT served as usage by the dispatcher (escape-hatch contract).
evidence: Docstring claims: "``--`` remains the escape hatch" (line 11)
Only pure-function coverage exists: `(['--', '--help'], False)` and `(['task', '--', '-h'], False)` in test_wants_help_scans_before_the_terminator (lines 101-102)

ABSENCE: no case in test_help_anywhere_before_terminator_shows_usage_no_write or a sibling drives `_cli.main(["create", "task", "--", ...])` to assert the dispatcher does not print usage / does perform the handler path
advisory.finding: The `--` terminator escape-hatch is asserted as a repaired-contract behavior in the test module docstring but is only covered at the `_wants_help` pure-function level; no end-to-end `_cli.main` test verifies that a help flag AFTER `--` (e.g. `create task -- --help`) is NOT intercepted as usage and instead flows to the handler as data.
scenarios: A future change to _wants_help or the dispatcher call site that mishandles the `--` terminator would still pass the end-to-end suite, since the escape-hatch behavior is only guarded by the isolated pure-function test.
